content.text: {"headline":"Approve 'No action' (P0): no intraday change is needed right now, at no extra cost.","why":"The general queue had a sick wave: 9 absences against a usual 2.4 per day (4 called in sick, 5 sent home unwell, the last at 14:20). Call volume is normal at 564 calls against 568 forecast, so this was a staffing shortfall, not a demand spike. Between 12:30 and 13:30 only 27–30 agents were on the phones against 30–33 planned, and service level dropped as low as 29.7%. From 13:45, 33–34 agents were on the phones against 32 planned, which suggests cover has recovered. The model predicts 100% service level on both payments and general, 0% abandons and 100% for the rest of the day, all at INR 0 extra cost. That is above the 80% target with no policy issues.","trade_offs":["No alternative plans were generated, so there is nothing to compare on cost or customer impact. P0 is the only option and costs nothing.","No staff are moved between queues, so there is no risk to the payments queue.","Diagnosis confidence is medium. The detector's figure of 51 vs 57.6 agents does not match the attendance log, and the disruption window shows as 20:00–20:00, which means the model sees no remaining gap. If the detector's view is the right one, doing nothing could leave the general queue short."],"watch":"Check live agents on the general queue against the plan, and watch its service level over the next 30–60 minutes. If more people are sent home, or service level drops toward 80%, re-run the plan. Also confirm which agent count is correct: the attendance log (33–34 on the phones) or the detector (51 vs 57.6)."}
